comment: Verification contract for T-007 (high, tdd per the risk-gate-matrix high-tier row). stack: shell waives lint/typecheck/build. unit-tests / acceptance-tests carry TDD red_evidence (the panel-round-6 RED captures, 341/4 in both runtimes against the pre-fix resolver -- the red that matches the shipped, post-remediation code) and green_evidence (395/0 in both runtimes -- the ONE statement of this tally in this comment); the sh capture is the unit check, the pwsh capture the acceptance check, together proving both runtimes. That single statement is deliberate, and it is deliberate because stating it twice has now failed twice: round 11 left this contract at 355 while its captures said 356, and round 15 left it at a number its own captures had already moved past -- three times over, inside the very sentence that claimed the number was stated once. The tally is not restated below; read it from the declared green_evidence captures. Round 7 closed the Anthropic panelist's Major: AC-059/TEST-059 (ruling E, 2026-08-28) had been written into requirements.md, acceptance-tests.md, traceability.md and this task's Done When, but never implemented -- a repository grep for AC-059, TEST-059 and the three approval-surface path literals returned zero hits outside the spec documents. TEST-059 now exists in this task's own suite as the registration-time deny-list grep AC-059 specifies (scanned set: the Resolver alone, all three of resolve-project-context.{py,sh,ps1}, plus every live twin that exists -- none do yet, this package is staged for a human to apply), contributing eleven assertions, counted from the log rather than from memory. Its non-vacuity is proved by mutation rather than by a suite-level RED, because a test-only addition has no failing production state to capture: verification/T-007/mutation-proofs.log injects one mention of each of the three surfaces into the staged Resolver, records TEST-059 failing with all three categories named, and restores the file to its exact shipped sha256. Round 8 then closed the OpenAI panelist's Critical: _rollback_transaction rolled resolver-evidence.yaml back along with the publication artifacts on the post-publication-mismatch path (Evidence commits last, and the rollback set was entries[:count]), against REQ-001 step (m)'s explicit rule that the subject is the three publication artifacts and never resolver-evidence.yaml. Evidence is now excluded from the rollback set and from the count the diagnostic reports; the same mutation log carries that second mutant, which the post-publication case kills. Rounds 9 to 12 then closed a second OpenAI Critical (the journal was deleted before the Block record was durable), the owner's rulings (a) and (b), and a third OpenAI Major that ruling (b) itself exposed: with a leaf symlink now acceptable, _repo_relative resolved the whole path and the journal recorded the symlink's referent while the commit replaced the lexical entry, so a rollback restored the referent and left the published bytes standing. _repo_relative_target records the lexical entry, by the same parent-resolve rule the containment check uses, and round 12 added the leaf-symlink fixture that had been missing -- five assertions, and mutant E kills it. Round 13 then closed a further OpenAI Major: the round-9 deferral guarded the journal's deletion on whether the ROLLBACK completed, not on whether the Block record became durable, so the journal was discarded even when the Evidence write had failed; _block_reporting now returns (exit_code, wrote_evidence) and both post-publication branches discard only when complete and wrote, with _block kept as a thin wrapper so its forty call sites are unchanged. Round 15 then closed both remaining panel findings with fixtures rather than disclosures. The OpenAI Major was a live defect: _recover_journal validated each journal entry's path and uniqueness but never that the SET was a bundle this Resolver could have written, so an attacker-committed journal naming two genuinely in-set targets could classify a live artifact as committed and have the MIX rollback unlink it; _legitimate_journal_bundles now requires the Full track's three targets or the Lite track's two, and mutant G kills the new fixture on four assertions. The Anthropic Minor was a correction of this task's own disclosure: mutant C was reachable after all, using the kill hook the suite already ships, and the fixture now exists. The mutation log carries nineteen mutants, all against the shipped bytes, with a clean control run at the top: every mutant except F, O and Q is killed; F, O and Q stay at the control tally and are labelled UNCOVERED in the log itself, each with its argument stated there. F is the Evidence-write-fails-after-completed-rollback combination a panelist has verified as unconstructable. O is the unlink-side directory fsync, and its UNCOVERED reason is now a measured obstacle rather than an impossibility claim: plant_sentinels writes all three publication artifacts before every fixture, so no rollback in this suite reaches the ABSENT branch that carries the barrier, and three fixture attempts on round 25 were withdrawn. Reaching it needs a fixture whose PRE state omits an artifact -- open work, not a proof. M -- which this comment once placed in that category -- was disproved on round 22, the third false-unreachability claim in this task, and its kill was then found on round 24 to have been happening for the WRONG REASON (the overlay retained closed directory descriptor numbers, the kernel reused one for a temp file, and the injection was firing on a file fsync; a stack-trace probe located it and the overlay now discards descriptors on close, after which the injection provably never fires under M at all): the round-22 fault-injection fixture (publication-fsync-failure, an os.open/os.fsync overlay failing the feature directory's first barrier exactly once) makes the fsync CALL observable even though its durability effect is not, and both M and the round-20 counting fix (mutant N) now die against it. The same round fixed an unguarded diagnostics[0] index in that fixture which mutant M had exposed by crashing the driver. D's coverage arrived on round 19, after a panelist disproved the claim that no fixture could graft a journal across batch directories -- the second of this task's own unreachability claims shown wrong by the panel (C was the first). F's impossibility argument is the one a panelist has verified and endorsed: every route to a failed Evidence write fails during Prepare, so committed==0 and the guarded branch cannot be entered. H, I and J are the report's own mutations (a), (b) and (c), re-run under the current harness after round 16 found the report citing them with no capture behind them anywhere in the bundle; (d) is labelled not-re-verified rather than restated. K covers the round-17 read-containment fix. Both remaining uncovered guards sit on the rollback/Evidence/journal path, whose correctness there rests on review rather than on regression tests -- stated because a contract that declares required checks passed should also say where its evidence stops. The nine sibling regression suites were re-run at these bytes (631 passing, 0 failing). regression covers the nine sibling suites at the shipped state: resolver-evidence-schema 20/0, match 125/0, cli 13/0, discovery 24/0, lite 18/0, validate-resolver-evidence 138/0, parity 70/0, metamorphic 150/0, component-path-resolver 73/0 (631 passing, 0 failing). requirement-traceability runs check-traceability against the feature's traceability.json (8 links, exit 0). check-component-coverage is not carried as a contract check: this repository has no sdd/project-context.yaml, so the gate is in disabled-legacy state and check-contract's CAPABILITY_STATE_GATED_IDS predicate does not activate the tier-minimum requirement (its verdict record was still captured for the record at verification/qg/T-007/component-coverage.log, state 'not-applicable (disabled-legacy)', exit 0); this matches sibling tasks T-008/T-009/T-010. cross_model is 'required' rather than omitted because this task's tasks.md entry carries Security-Sensitive: true, which sdd-ship Step 4 makes a hard pre-gate requirement; the cross-model-verification check is DEFAULT-FAIL here and stays passes:false until a fresh panel round has run against the shipped bytes and check-cross-model has written the aggregate at verification/T-007.cross-model.json. spec_revision is the current requirements+design+acceptance-tests concatenation hash. Q is the round-26 revert of the Evidence-durability propagation: reaching it needs the Evidence write's own directory fsync to fail inside a run that is already Blocking, and the existing fault-injection overlays are single-shot and fire earlier. That is the measured obstacle, recorded as open work -- this task has offered four impossibility proofs (C, D, M, O) and all four were wrong. R is the round-27 revert of the AC-014 fix -- it reinstates a `capability-resolver: warning:` line whose token is absent from REQ-002's closed sixteen-value enum -- and it is KILLED by a source-level assertion that scans the shipped resolver for every literal diagnostic prefix it writes, so a line no fixture reaches is still bound by AC-014. S is the round-28 revert of the post-Block Evidence classification: without it a journal left behind by a Block that FOLLOWED a completed rollback is read as the unrecoverable third state, because Evidence legitimately holds the Block record rather than either recorded generation, and a transient unlink failure at that instant would Block every future invocation forever. It dies against a planted-journal fixture that asserts the scan converges and discards.
